entry.title: Writing a Domain Model in Ruby Without Using class
entry.summary:
Introduction
From Ruby 3.2, the Data class has been introduced, allowing us to explore ways of representing domain models without using class. In this article, I’ll examine how we can do that. When writing business logic in Ruby, we naturally tend to use class. We set attributes in initialize, and change state via instance methods. Especially if you’ve been writing Rails code, this feels natural. However, whether managing logic with a stateful class is suitable for every case is debatable. For domain logic where we want to avoid side effects, class-based design might not always be optimal.
